questions.stemHtml: A 3-year-old child is brought to the clinic because of walking difficulties. His mother says he has always walked on his toes and walks by tilting side-to-side. He also has progressive muscle weakness. There is no history of trauma, fever, or rash. On examination, calf hypertrophy with atrophied thigh muscles is noted as shown below. There is no tenderness on palpation. What is the most probable diagnosis?
